jobs.title: Affordable Housing Finance Product Manager - Executive Director
jobs.description:
Morgan Stanley Community Development Finance is seeking a senior-level Affordable Housing Finance Product Manager to lead the end-to-end management of the Firm’s affordable housing private equity investment portfolio. The role will oversee the full investment lifecycle—from sourcing and origination through underwriting, transaction approval, closing, portfolio and asset management, governance, risk monitoring, performance reporting, and investment exits.

This individual will serve as a senior product owner and relationship manager for affordable housing private equity strategies, working closely with internal stakeholders, fund managers, sponsors, legal counsel, risk partners, and other control functions to ensure disciplined execution, strong portfolio performance, and alignment with Morgan Stanley’s community development, risk management, and business objectives.

Note: Location is open within the the U.S.

Responsibilities

Oversee the affordable housing private equity product strategy and portfolio management framework, including origination priorities, investment guidelines, portfolio objectives, performance targets, and exit planning.
Lead sourcing and originations for new affordable housing private equity investment opportunities, including evaluation of fund managers, sponsors, markets, investment structures, projected returns, community development impact, and strategic fit.
Oversee due diligence, underwriting, financial analysis, market review, sponsor and guarantor assessment, legal documentation, and transaction approval materials for new investments and follow-on commitments.
Present investment opportunities, portfolio updates, risk matters, and strategic recommendations to transaction council, senior management, credit partners, and other internal governance forums.
Serve as the primary relationship manager for affordable housing private equity fund managers, developers, sponsors, and other external partners, ensuring strong communication, accountability, and execution.
Manage post-closing portfolio oversight, periodic asset reviews, compliance monitoring, operating performance analysis, capital account tracking, distribution forecasting, valuation support, and watchlist management.
Monitor fund and underlying asset performance against underwriting expectations, investment agreements, regulatory requirements, and CRA objectives.
Represent Morgan Stanley on fund advisory boards, investor committees, and other governance bodies, providing guidance on consents, amendments, waivers, workouts, dispositions, and other material portfolio matters.
Partner with internal risk stake holders to ensure appropriate controls, approvals, reporting, and issue resolution.
Lead, mentor, and develop staff supporting affordable housing private equity products, promoting strong execution standards, analytical rigor, and consistent portfolio management practices.

Skills Required

Deep understanding of affordable housing finance, private equity fund structures, LIHTC investments, multi-family real estate underwriting, asset management, and portfolio risk management.
Strong financial modeling, valuation, credit analysis, cash flow forecasting, and investment performance assessment skills.
Proven ability to evaluate complex transactions, identify risks, develop mitigation strategies, and make sound investment recommendations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex investment, risk, and portfolio matters clearly to senior management and governance committees.
Strong relationship management and negotiation skills with demonstrated ability to work effectively with fund managers, developers, sponsors, legal counsel, and internal control partners.
Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities, transactions, portfolio matters, and deadlines in a complex institutional environment.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word; experience with portfolio reporting systems, investment databases, and data visualization tools preferred.

Experience

15+ years of relevant experience in affordable housing finance, private equity, multi-family real estate investment, asset management, credit, or portfolio management.
Demonstrated experience managing investments across the full lifecycle, including origination, underwriting, approval, closing, construction or stabilization monitoring, ongoing asset management, workouts or restructurings, and exits.
Experience with public sector financing sources and regulatory frameworks, including Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, HUD/FHA programs, tax-exempt bonds, state and local housing programs, and other community development tools.
Established relationships with affordable housing developers, fund managers, lenders, investors, public agencies, and other industry participants preferred.
Prior experience leading teams, managing senior stakeholder relationships, and operating within a regulated financial institution or similarly complex investment platform strongly preferred.

What You Can Expect From Morgan Stanley

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.

To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices into your browser.

New York

jobs.title: Executive Director, Real Estate - Asset Manager, Industrials
jobs.description:
Morgan Stanley Investment Management, together with its investment advisory affiliates, has more than 1,300 investment professionals around the world and $2 trillion in assets under management or supervision as of June 30, 2026. Morgan Stanley Investment Management strives to provide outstanding long-term investment performance, service, and a comprehensive suite of investment management solutions to a diverse client base, which includes governments, institutions, corporations and individuals worldwide. For further information about Morgan Stanley Investment Management, please visit www.morganstanley.com/im.   

Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing (“MSREI”) is the global private real estate investment management business of Morgan Stanley. One of the most active property investors in the world for over three decades, MSREI employs a patient, disciplined approach through global value-add / opportunistic and regional core / core-plus real estate investment strategies.

With 17 offices throughout the U.S., Europe and Asia, regional teams of dedicated real estate professionals combine a unique global perspective with local presence and significant transaction execution expertise. MSREI currently manages $58 billion of gross real estate assets worldwide on behalf of its clients.

MSREI is seeking a highly experienced industrial real estate asset manager to be based in New York and oversee a significant portion of MSREI’s industrial portfolio across its various fund strategies.

You will assume responsibility for a strategically important, multi-market industrial portfolio of approximately $3 billion in Gross Asset Value (GAV); comprising roughly 70 assets totaling over 14.5 million square feet and approximately 130 tenancies across six major U.S. markets. This role represents one of the business’s largest dedicated industrial asset management positions.

As the successful candidate you will be expected to optimize portfolio performance by leveraging direct tenant relationships to drive leasing and retention, actively managing brokers to deliver leasing goals, and holding property management accountable for quality of operations.

Morgan Stanley Since 1935, Morgan Stanley is known as a global leader in financial services, continuously evolving and innovating to better serve our clients and our communities in more than 40 countries around the world.

What You’ll Do In The Role

Develop and execute asset-level business plans focused on maximizing value and operating performance.
Drive portfolio performance through leasing execution, tenant retention, capital planning, and revenue optimization.
Monitor asset performance against underwriting and investment objectives.
Lead leasing strategy across approximately 3.5 million square feet of near-term roll.
Coordinate closely with leasing brokers to establish market strategy, pricing, marketing, and transaction execution.
Negotiate lease agreements with tenants.
Manage property managers, leasing professionals, construction managers, and third-party service providers to ensure execution of business plans.
Coordinate capital projects and repositioning initiatives where appropriate.
Prepare and present investment recommendations and leasing approvals.
Lead quarterly asset reviews and annual business planning.
Monitor market fundamentals, competitive positioning, tenant demand, and valuation trends.
Identify opportunities to enhance portfolio value through leasing, redevelopment, or disposition.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

The role demands a highly organized, execution-oriented asset manager with substantial hands-on experience managing industrial assets. The ideal candidate is experienced working through the complex challenges that arise across a portfolio of this scale, overseeing capital improvement projects and repairs, and building and managing tenant relationships. Above all, this individual will drive accountability across internal and external stakeholders while maintaining a relentless focus on leasing performance and value creation.

Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science required.
10+ years of commercial real estate experience with significant industrial asset management responsibility.
Proven experience leading leasing strategy for large industrial portfolios.
Strong understanding of industrial market dynamics across multiple U.S. regions.
Experience managing third-party property managers and leasing brokers.
Excellent financial analysis, valuation, and investment decision-making skills.
Ability to prioritize competing initiatives across numerous assets simultaneously.
Strong communication and organizational leadership capabilities.

Posting Context Statement

Position Overview:

As the state's land-grant university, the University of Idaho develops solutions for complex problems facing our society. The university is establishing the Energy Institute to produce the next generation of energy leaders focused on the importance of agile energy portfolio analysis and transitions. In collaboration with industry partners, the institute will strengthen the nation's energy future and workforce talent pipeline by integrating robust engineering design coursework and research into regional energy solutions. With partnerships across the region, the Energy Institute performs multi-discipline research that supports clean, reliable, affordable energy while delivering energy literacy education for students and professionals.

The Executive Director of the Energy Institute will provide institutional vision, strategy, and leadership in educational programming, research innovation, workforce development, outreach, special projects, and advocacy in the domain of energy. Reporting to the Dean of the College of Engineering in collaboration with the Office of the President, the Executive Director will provide strategic leadership in developing and recommending key goals and actions to advance energy literacy and awareness, practical solutions to gain energy independence, and sustainable (safe, reliable, economical, renewable, clean) access to energy resources. The Executive Director will work closely with an academic leadership committee, an industry advisory board, faculty, and staff to identify, develop, implement, and promote energy programming that advances the core values and strategic priorities of the university in keeping with the needs of the energy industry.

Required Experience

15 years of progressive leadership experience in the energy industry, utilities, or closely related organizations
Building partnerships and coalitions resulting in shared actions and outcomes
Experience influencing change in a complex, decentralized organization with sizeable budget, scope, and personnel
Proposal development leading to external funding
Leading teams to completion of project objectives on scope, on schedule, and on budget
Experience with utility operating environment, including regulatory, environmental, and workforce issues
Experience in the energy sector and/or energy discipline and commitment to championing energy-related causes
Collaborating with multiple entities across different sectors to deepen the public's understanding and appreciation of energy production, research, and security

Required Education

Bachelor's Degree in engineering from an ABET accredited university
Master's Degree in engineering, business administration or energy studies from an accredited university

Required Other

Professional Engineer (PE) license from Idaho or ability to obtain an Idaho PE license within the first year of hire
Completion of, or ability to complete, the University of Idaho Energy Executive Course or similar program within the first year of hire

Experience

Additional Preferred:

Demonstrated leadership of teams without direct supervisory oversight
Demonstrated skills in negotiation and conflict resolution
Experience with surveys, data collection, data analysis, and data visualization
Technical knowledge and skills related to energy, utilities, engineering, energy economics, etc.
Electric power industry experience
Non-profit board leadership experience
Experience should include industry, higher education, or government leadership – or a combination thereof
Recognized, high-level influence with a deep understanding of key issues in the energy sector
Experience with the integration of nuclear power generation into electric transmission and distribution systems

Education

PhD or terminal degree in energy, engineering, business administration, or economics or master's degree with 25 years in the energy industry
Experience working or collaborating in higher education

new_jobs.description:
Morgan Stanley Investment Management, together with its investment advisory affiliates, has more than 1,300 investment professionals around the world and $2 trillion in assets under management or supervision as of June 30, 2026. Morgan Stanley Investment Management strives to provide outstanding long-term investment performance, service, and a comprehensive suite of investment management solutions to a diverse client base, which includes governments, institutions, corporations and individuals worldwide. For further information about Morgan Stanley Investment Management, please visit www.morganstanley.com/im.   

Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing (“MSREI”) is the global private real estate investment management business of Morgan Stanley. One of the most active property investors in the world for over three decades, MSREI employs a patient, disciplined approach through global value-add / opportunistic and regional core / core-plus real estate investment strategies.

With 17 offices throughout the U.S., Europe and Asia, regional teams of dedicated real estate professionals combine a unique global perspective with local presence and significant transaction execution expertise. MSREI currently manages $58 billion of gross real estate assets worldwide on behalf of its clients.

MSREI is seeking a highly experienced industrial real estate asset manager to be based in New York and oversee a significant portion of MSREI’s industrial portfolio across its various fund strategies.

You will assume responsibility for a strategically important, multi-market industrial portfolio of approximately $3 billion in Gross Asset Value (GAV); comprising roughly 70 assets totaling over 14.5 million square feet and approximately 130 tenancies across six major U.S. markets. This role represents one of the business’s largest dedicated industrial asset management positions.

As the successful candidate you will be expected to optimize portfolio performance by leveraging direct tenant relationships to drive leasing and retention, actively managing brokers to deliver leasing goals, and holding property management accountable for quality of operations.

Morgan Stanley Since 1935, Morgan Stanley is known as a global leader in financial services, continuously evolving and innovating to better serve our clients and our communities in more than 40 countries around the world.

What You’ll Do In The Role

Develop and execute asset-level business plans focused on maximizing value and operating performance.
Drive portfolio performance through leasing execution, tenant retention, capital planning, and revenue optimization.
Monitor asset performance against underwriting and investment objectives.
Lead leasing strategy across approximately 3.5 million square feet of near-term roll.
Coordinate closely with leasing brokers to establish market strategy, pricing, marketing, and transaction execution.
Negotiate lease agreements with tenants.
Manage property managers, leasing professionals, construction managers, and third-party service providers to ensure execution of business plans.
Coordinate capital projects and repositioning initiatives where appropriate.
Prepare and present investment recommendations and leasing approvals.
Lead quarterly asset reviews and annual business planning.
Monitor market fundamentals, competitive positioning, tenant demand, and valuation trends.
Identify opportunities to enhance portfolio value through leasing, redevelopment, or disposition.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

The role demands a highly organized, execution-oriented asset manager with substantial hands-on experience managing industrial assets. The ideal candidate is experienced working through the complex challenges that arise across a portfolio of this scale, overseeing capital improvement projects and repairs, and building and managing tenant relationships. Above all, this individual will drive accountability across internal and external stakeholders while maintaining a relentless focus on leasing performance and value creation.

Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science required.
10+ years of commercial real estate experience with significant industrial asset management responsibility.
Proven experience leading leasing strategy for large industrial portfolios.
Strong understanding of industrial market dynamics across multiple U.S. regions.
Experience managing third-party property managers and leasing brokers.
Excellent financial analysis, valuation, and investment decision-making skills.
Ability to prioritize competing initiatives across numerous assets simultaneously.
Strong communication and organizational leadership capabilities.
